title: A genome-wide in vivo CRISPR screen identifies neuroprotective strategies in the mouse and human retina
authors: Ning Shen, Michael J. Fitzpatrick, Ellen G. Harding, Sohini Rebba, Florentina Soto, Philip A. Ruzycki, Daniel Kerschensteiner
abstract: Shen et al. combine a genome-wide CRISPR screen in mice with an adult human retina model to identify broadly protective gene therapies for retinitis pigmentosa. They show that boosting UFD1 or UXT preserves photoreceptors and vision by helping the retina withstand stress from misfolded proteins.

title: SARM1 executes neuronal parthanatos and promotes excitotoxic cell death
authors: Tong Wu, Liya Yuan, Yo Sasaki, Si Jia Chen, William Buchser, A. Joseph Bloom, Aaron DiAntonio, Jeffrey Milbrandt
abstract: Wu et al. show that PARP1 hyperactivation activates the NAD⁺ hydrolase SARM1 to execute neuronal parthanatos. SARM1 drives mitochondrial depolarization, AIF translocation, and neuronal death following DNA damage and other parthanatos-associated insults. These findings expand the therapeutic potentia…

title: A bidirectional brain-fat body axis for pathogen avoidance
authors: Yujie Wang, Jean-François De Backer, Aurélie Muria, Ayako Abe, Kokoro Saito, Helen Holvoet, Mareike Selcho, Hiromu Tanimoto, Ilona C. Grunwald Kadow
abstract: How immune tissues influence brain function remains unclear. Wang et al. show that pathogen sensing recruits neuromodulatory input to the fat body, triggering fat body-derived dopamine release that modulates mushroom body output neurons to drive pathogen avoidance.

title: Macrophage-mediated refinement of the dural lymphatic regulates social behavior
authors: Gabriel A. Tavares, Liam O’Reilly, Natalie M. Frederick, David A. Shapiro, Ashleigh Vicchiarelli, Megan Sullivan, Nathan Jiang, Maximillian Mattes, Coby Goelz, Nnadozie Uchegbu, Haley Brown, Joseph Lubera, Laura Wolfe, Brendan T. Boylan, Cornelia Bergmann, Tara M. DeSilva, Antoine Louveau
abstract: The dural lymphatics contribute to brain maintenance. Tavares et al. identify a macrophage-dependent refinement of the lymphatic vasculature during normal development. The availability of growth factors, cell death, and phagocytosis all act in the refinement of the lymphatics. Failure to refine thes…

title: Astrocytic glucose metabolism regulates the survival of newborn hippocampal neurons in the adult brain
authors: Xinxing Wang, Lu Chen, Thomas A. Kim, Zhiyi Wang, Xike Peng, Michelle D. Syty, Faye Wang, Yuhan Zhang, Patrick Wehrle, Yusuke Nasu, Qiaojie Xiong, Shaoyu Ge
abstract: Environmental exploration prompts astrocytes to convert glucose into lactate, which supports the survival of newborn neurons in the adult hippocampus. This study identifies a metabolic partnership that links experience-driven brain activity to the survival of new neurons in the adult brain.

title: Top-down control of the descending pain modulatory system drives multimodal placebo analgesia
authors: Giulia Livrizzi, Janie Chang-Weinberg, Desiree A. Johnson, Susan T. Lubejko, Jingzhu Liao, Blake A. Kimmey, Chunyang Dong, Yuan Li, Kevin T. Beier, Gregory Corder, Lin Tian, Matthew R. Banghart
abstract: Livrizzi, Chang-Weinberg, et al. identify a cortical-brainstem circuit that mediates top-down control of pain during placebo analgesia and find that pain relief is gated by endogenous opioids in the vlPAG. They find that the placebo effect extends to multiple forms of pain and that pre-conditioning…

title: Infant learning forms lasting memory schemas that influence adult behavior
authors: Benjamin Bessières, Emmanuel Prikas, Sebastian Goodwin-Groen, Leonardo Silenzi, Cristina M. Alberini
abstract: Bessières, Prikas, et al. report that episodic-like learning in infant mice establishes enduring memory schemas that guide adult behavior. The schema facilitates relearning and the formation of new, congruent memories in adulthood. Infantile schemas undergo hippocampus-dependent systems consolidatio…

title: Human hippocampal ripples prioritize model-based learning
authors: Xiaoyu Zhou, Xiongfei Wang, Xiangyu Hu, Haiteng Wang, Jinbo Zhang, Qianqian Yu, Jiahua Xu, Zhibing Xiao, Li He, Yunzhe Liu
abstract: Zhou et al. show how the human brain learns efficiently from sparse experience. Hippocampal ripples coordinate with the frontopolar cortex, a region at the apex of the frontal brain, to transform direct experience into learning that generalizes to related situations.

title: Cell-type-specific APOE4 cascade across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum
authors: David Shostak, Zherui Liang, Yadong Huang
abstract: Shostak et al. propose a cell-type-specific APOE4 cascade across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum, where neuronal APOE4 upregulation during aging initiates damage and triggers glial responses that, alongside glial APOE4, amplify neurodegeneration, highlighting temporal dynamics that guide stage- an…

title: The oracle and the didact: Orbitofrontal influences on learning and dopaminergic error signaling
abstract: The orbitofrontal cortex influences behavior by representing internal models of the causal structure of the world. In this perspective, Schoenbaum and Kahnt argue that this function also supports learning by shaping error signaling in midbrain dopamine neurons and other brain areas.

title: A hypothalamic circuit for anticipating future changes in energy balance
authors: Samuel J. Walker, Elijah D. Lowenstein, Amelia M. Douglass, Callum M.P. Thomas, Joseph C. Madara, Hakan Kucukdereli, Eunice A. Barbosa-Meillon, Jenkang Tao, Jon M. Resch, Bradford B. Lowell
abstract: Walker, Lowenstein, et al. demonstrate that hunger neurons in the mouse hypothalamus are rapidly activated not only by actual energy deficit but also by environmental cues predicting future fasting. This predictive hunger signal is conveyed by upstream Sim2-expressing neurons, revealing that the bra…

title: Sculpting functional brain drainage
abstract: Mechanisms directing meningeal lymphatic development have remained largely unexplored. Tavares et al. identify macrophage-mediated sculpting as a developmental program that establishes cerebrospinal fluid drainage pathways, revealing how disrupted lymphatic maturation may contribute to neurodevelopm…

title: Hunger that runs ahead of the body
abstract: In this issue of Neuron, Walker, Lowenstein et al. identify PVHSim2 neurons as excitatory input that rapidly activates ARCAgRP hunger neurons. By tracking predicted food availability, these cells help the brain anticipate an energy deficit before the body registers one.

title: Aggregation and propagation of TAF15 trigger neurodegeneration
authors: Lanxia Meng, Congcong Liu, Huangchuan Gong, Yan Gao, Meihui Li, Han Liu, Hanying Teng, Min Xiong, Hui Liu, Mingmin Yan, Dae Ki Hong, Seong Su Kang, Jing Xiong, Zhentao Zhang
abstract: Meng et al. report that TAF15 forms amyloid fibrils capable of propagation both in vitro and in vivo. The spread of TAF15 pathology triggers progressive neurodegeneration, cognitive impairment, and anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. These findings establish TAF15 aggregation as a key pathogenic…
